answer: Each proposed identity must finish a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings before it can produce a Wesolowski proof. Because each square depends on the previous result, a GPU cannot parallelize one identity’s chain; it can run separate chains for multiple clones, but each consumes compute and must still wait its own delay. This makes mass Sybil creation costly and time-bound, like opening vaults one at a time on an island while a sparrow waits.
